body:
An anti join whose preserved side is small and whose other side is large ("accounts in this region that have no event", `small EXCEPT big`, an `ANTI JOIN` against a fact table) is flipped by the build side optimizer into a RIGHT ANTI join: the small side is built, the large side probes. The probe rows of a RIGHT ANTI join are never emitted, they only mark build rows as matched, and the join returns the build rows that were not marked. A probe row whose key does not occur on the build side cannot mark anything, so it does not have to reach the join at all. That is exactly the situation join filter pushdown exists for, and it already handles RIGHT SEMI joins this way, but `JoinFilterPushdownUtil::JoinTypeIsSupported` rejected RIGHT ANTI together with ANTI ("FIXME: anti/right_anti - we could do this, but need to invert the join conditions"). The inversion is only needed for a plain ANTI join, whose unmatched probe rows are the result. For RIGHT ANTI the build keys can be pushed into the probe side as they are.

This PR makes RIGHT ANTI a supported join type of join filter pushdown:

`JOIN_FILTER_PUSHDOWN` generates the filters (min/max, IN list, bloom filter, as for any other join) for RIGHT ANTI comparison joins, including the filters that are pushed into a materialized CTE on the probe side.

With several equality keys the join gets the per-column bloom or prefix-range filters of #28726 under the same condition as any other join (build side at most 5% of the estimated probe side), and a scan that #28768 lets wait for a small filter producer waits for a RIGHT ANTI join as it does for a RIGHT SEMI join.

Plain ANTI joins stay unsupported. The choice of the build side is not changed: `BUILD_SIDE_PROBE_SIDE` does not give RIGHT ANTI the dynamic filter bonus it gives RIGHT SEMI. An ANTI join with a small filtered preserved side is flipped by the size comparison already, and I found no case in which the bonus alone decides the orientation (it needs a preserved side that is at least 64 times smaller in rows than the scan on the other side and still more expensive to build). Nothing changes in the executor: the hash join already publishes its filters independently of the join type.

### Preconditions

* the join is a RIGHT ANTI comparison join (i.e. an ANTI join that the build side optimizer flipped);
* everything `JOIN_FILTER_PUSHDOWN` requires for the other join types: the probe-side key expressions are not volatile, and the filter is only pushed through operators and into scans that accept it.

The filters are part of `JOIN_FILTER_PUSHDOWN`: `SET disabled_optimizers = 'join_filter_pushdown'` disables them together with all other join filters.

### Example

```sql
CREATE TABLE accounts AS SELECT i AS id, i % 50 AS region, i % 7 AS tier FROM range(2000000) t(i);
CREATE TABLE events AS SELECT (i * 31) % 3000000 AS account_id, i % 365 AS day, i % 97 AS amount FROM range(60000000) t(i);

SELECT count(*) FROM accounts a ANTI JOIN events e ON a.id = e.account_id WHERE a.region = 7 AND a.tier = 3;
```

`EXPLAIN ANALYZE`, before:

```
HASH_JOIN    Join Type: RIGHT_ANTI; Conditions: account_id = id
  TABLE_SCAN events    Projections: account_id                                             60,000,000 rows
  TABLE_SCAN accounts  Filters: region = 7, tier = 3                                            5,714 rows
```

After:

```
HASH_JOIN    Join Type: RIGHT_ANTI; Conditions: account_id = id
  TABLE_SCAN events    Projections: account_id; Dynamic Filters: optional: account_id IN PRF(id)  114,280 rows
  TABLE_SCAN accounts  Filters: region = 7, tier = 3                                               5,714 rows
```

User-mode instructions at one thread (`perf stat -e instructions:u`, median of 3, release build, `main` vs. this PR):

| query | main | this PR | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ANTI JOIN` (above) | 3.19e9 | 2.14e9 | 0.67 |
| `SELECT id FROM accounts WHERE region = 7 AND tier = 3 EXCEPT SELECT account_id FROM events` | 3.18e9 | 2.13e9 | 0.67 |

A `NOT EXISTS` over the same tables does not change: it is decorrelated into a different plan that already restricts the scan of `events`.

### Regression check

Without vs. with the change on TPC-H and TPC-DS (SF1 and SF10), JOB and ClickBench: the results are identical at 1 and 32 threads (TPC-H / TPC-DS SF1), and no `EXPLAIN` plan changes (join filters are not part of the plan text, and no join changes sides). 3 of the 121 TPC-H / TPC-DS queries have a RIGHT ANTI join; their instructions at one thread are between 0.97x and 1.02x. There is none in JOB or ClickBench.

### Tests

`test/optimizer/pushdown/join_filter_pushdown_right_anti.test` (new): `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` pins that the probe scan of a RIGHT ANTI join gets `Dynamic Filters` (also next to an inequality between the two sides), that a plain ANTI join, a volatile probe key and `disabled_optimizers = 'join_filter_pushdown'` give none, and results for NULL keys on either side with `=` and `IS NOT DISTINCT FROM`, `NOT IN`, duplicate build keys, two equality keys, VARCHAR keys, an empty probe side, an empty build side, an anti join below an outer join, over an aggregate, over a materialized CTE (one consumer, two anti join consumers whose filters are combined, and an anti join next to an unfiltered consumer), `EXCEPT`, and inside a recursive CTE. For joins on several keys it pins the per-column filters (the same as for the RIGHT SEMI join, min/max only above the 5% bound) and the results with NULLs in either key column on both sides for `=`, `IS NOT DISTINCT FROM` and a mix of the two, and that a scan below an aggregate on the probe side waits for the filter and the query still completes with an empty build side.

No existing expected plan changes. The tests in `test/optimizer`, `test/sql/join`, `test/sql/subquery`, `test/sql/aggregate`, `test/sql/optimizer`, `test/sql/cte`, `test/sql/setops`, `test/sql/sql_export` and the TPC-H / TPC-DS SF1 answer tests pass, `test/optimizer` and `test/sql/subquery` also with `debug_verify_column_bindings` enabled.

#28732 converts more `NOT EXISTS` / `NOT IN` joins into ANTI joins before join ordering, which produces more RIGHT ANTI joins for this change to act on.

This PR is independent of the other optimizer PRs I am opening next to it (#28786).

Note: this PR was generated by an AI coding agent; it is a draft pending review by the author.

comments.body: Done in 455e35e58e9: the `join_filter_right_anti` optimizer type is removed and RIGHT ANTI filters are generated as part of `join_filter_pushdown` (disabled together with it); the PR no longer touches `OptimizerType`, `enum_util.cpp` or any header, and the build side choice is unchanged.

review_comments.body: The new RIGHT ANTI build-side bonus is not covered by this test. It expects `RIGHT_ANTI` even with `join_filter_right_anti` disabled, so removing the bonus would still pass. Across preserved sides of 3,000 to 6,000,000 rows against a 2,000,000-row probe table, unfiltered and with filters on both sides, enabling the optimizer did not change the orientation. Could we pin a case where only the bonus flips the ANTI join, or is the bonus needed at all? This is a non-blocking question.

The single CTE reference leaves shared materialized-CTE filtering untested. That path combines filters from several consumers, which this query cannot exercise. With two RIGHT ANTI consumers, it materializes 6,073 of 909,092 rows and matches the disabled run. I would add both cases below to cover combined filters and ensure an unfiltered consumer still sees every CTE row. This is non-blocking.

```sql
query II
WITH m AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT * FROM big WHERE v < 5) SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM small s ANTI JOIN m ON s.k = m.k WHERE s.k < 500), (SELECT count(*) FROM other o ANTI JOIN m ON o.k = m.k WHERE o.k < 1000);
----
333	133

query II
WITH m AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT * FROM big WHERE v < 5) SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM small s ANTI JOIN m ON s.k = m.k WHERE s.k < 500), (SELECT count(*) FROM m);
----
333	909092
```

+# name: test/optimizer/pushdown/join_filter_pushdown_right_anti.test
+# description: RIGHT ANTI joins push join filters into their probe side
+# group: [pushdown]
+
+statement ok
+SET threads=4;
+
+statement ok
+CREATE TABLE small AS SELECT i::BIGINT AS k, (i % 7)::INTEGER AS v FROM range(2000) t(i);
+
+# every third key
+statement ok
+CREATE TABLE big AS SELECT ((i % 50000) * 3)::BIGINT AS k, (i % 11)::INTEGER AS v FROM range(2000000) t(i);
+
+statement ok
+CREATE TABLE small_null AS SELECT CASE WHEN i % 10 = 0 THEN NULL ELSE i END::BIGINT AS k, (i % 7)::INTEGER AS v FROM range(2000) t(i);
+
+statement ok
+CREATE TABLE big_null AS SELECT CASE WHEN i % 100 = 0 THEN NULL ELSE (i % 50000) * 3 END::BIGINT AS k, (i % 11)::INTEGER AS v FROM range(2000000) t(i);
+
+statement ok
+CREATE TABLE other AS SELECT i::BIGINT AS k, i * 10 AS w FROM range(0, 2000, 5) t(i);
+
+statement ok
+CREATE TABLE empty_big(k BIGINT, v INTEGER);
+
+statement ok
+CREATE TABLE small_str AS SELECT 'key_' || i AS k, (i % 7)::INTEGER AS v FROM range(2000) t(i);
+
+statement ok
+CREATE TABLE big_str AS SELECT 'key_' || ((i % 50000) * 3) AS k, (i % 11)::INTEGER AS v FROM range(2000000) t(i);
+
+query I
+SELECT name FROM duckdb_optimizers() WHERE name = 'join_filter_right_anti';
+----
+join_filter_right_anti
+
+# the anti join is flipped to RIGHT_ANTI (the small side is the build side) and the scan of the probe side gets the
+# build keys as a join filter
+query II
+EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT count(*), sum(s.k) FROM small s ANTI JOIN big b ON s.k = b.k WHERE s.k < 500;
+----
+analyzed_plan	<REGEX>:(?s).*Join Type: RIGHT_ANTI.*Table: \S+\.big.*Dynamic Filters:.*
+
+query II
+SELECT count(*), sum(s.k) FROM small s ANTI JOIN big b ON s.k = b.k WHERE s.k < 500;
+----
+333	83167
+
+# NOT EXISTS
+query II
+SELECT count(*), sum(s.k) FROM small s WHERE s.k < 500 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM big b WHERE b.k = s.k);
+----
+333	83167
+
+# NULL keys on the probe side never match: filtering them out changes nothing
+query II
+SELECT count(*), sum(s.k) FROM small s ANTI JOIN big_null b ON s.k = b.k WHERE s.k < 500;
+----
+335	83467
+
+# NULL keys on the build side have no match and are part of the result: the filter only removes probe rows
+query III
+SELECT count(*), count(s.k), sum(s.k) FROM small_null s ANTI JOIN big b ON s.k = b.k WHERE s.k < 500 OR s.k IS NULL;
+----
+500	300	74997
+
+# IS NOT DISTINCT FROM with NULLs on both sides: NULL matches NULL, the filter has to keep the NULL probe rows
+query III
+SELECT count(*), count(s.k), sum(s.k) FROM small_null s ANTI JOIN big_null b ON s.k IS NOT DISTINCT FROM b.k WHERE s.k < 500 OR s.k IS NULL;
+----
+300	300	74997
+
+query III
+SELECT count(*), count(s.k), sum(s.k) FROM small_null s ANTI JOIN big b ON s.k IS NOT DISTINCT FROM b.k WHERE s.k < 500 OR s.k IS NULL;
+----
+500	300	74997
+
+# NOT IN is a MARK join: NULLs on either side
+query II
+SELECT count(*), sum(s.k) FROM small s WHERE s.k < 500 AND s.k NOT IN (SELECT k FROM big);
+----
+333	83167
+
+query II
+SELECT count(*), sum(s.k) FROM small s WHERE s.k < 500 AND s.k NOT IN (SELECT k FROM big_null);
+----
+0	NULL
+
+# an additional inequality between the two sides: the filter is generated for the equality key only
+query II
+EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT count(*), sum(s.k) FROM small s ANTI JOIN big b ON s.k = b.k AND s.v <> b.v WHERE s.k < 500;
+----
+analyzed_plan	<REGEX>:(?s).*Join Type: RIGHT_ANTI.*Dynamic Filters:.*
+
+query II
+SELECT count(*), sum(s.k) FROM small s ANTI JOIN big b ON s.k = b.k AND s.v <> b.v WHERE s.k < 500;
+----
+333	83167
+
+# two equality keys
+query II
+SELECT count(*), sum(s.k) FROM small s ANTI JOIN big b ON s.k = b.k AND s.v = b.v WHERE s.k < 500;
+----
+333	83167
+
+# duplicate build keys
+query II
+SELECT count(*), sum(s.k) FROM (SELECT * FROM small UNION ALL SELECT * FROM small) s ANTI JOIN big b ON s.k = b.k WHERE s.k < 500;
+----
+666	166334
+
+# VARCHAR keys
+query II
+SELECT count(*), sum(s.v) FROM small_str s ANTI JOIN big_str b ON s.k = b.k WHERE s.v < 2;
+----
+381	191
+
+# an empty probe side: all build rows are returned
+query II
+SELECT count(*), sum(s.k) FROM small s ANTI JOIN empty_big b ON s.k = b.k WHERE s.k < 500;
+----
+500	124750
+
+# an empty build side
+query II
+SELECT count(*), sum(s.k) FROM small s ANTI JOIN big b ON s.k = b.k WHERE s.v = 99;
+----
+0	NULL
+
+# below an outer join
+query III
+SELECT count(*), count(o.w), sum(o.w) FROM (SELECT s.k FROM small s ANTI JOIN big b ON s.k = b.k WHERE s.k < 500) t LEFT JOIN other o ON t.k = o.k;
+----
+333	66	163350
+
+# the probe side is an aggregate
+query II
+SELECT count(*), sum(s.k) FROM small s ANTI JOIN (SELECT k, count(*) AS c FROM big GROUP BY k HAVING count(*) > 30) g ON s.k = g.k WHERE s.k < 500;
+----
+333	83167
+
+# the probe side is a materialized CTE
+query II
+WITH m AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT * FROM big WHERE v < 5) SELECT count(*), sum(s.k) FROM small s ANTI JOIN m ON s.k = m.k WHERE s.k < 500;

review_comments.body: Removed in c0f60803b66: the bonus would only decide the orientation for a preserved side at least 64 times smaller in rows than the other side's scan and still more expensive to build, which I could not produce either, so build_probe_side_optimizer.cpp is unchanged from main now and the optimizer type only controls filter generation.
Added both queries in c0f60803b66; they return `333 133` and `333 909092` with the optimizer enabled, and the same on a build without this change.

+SELECT count(*), sum(s.k) FROM (SELECT * FROM small UNION ALL SELECT * FROM small) s ANTI JOIN big b ON s.k = b.k WHERE s.k < 500;
+----
+666	166334
+
+# VARCHAR keys
+query II
+SELECT count(*), sum(s.v) FROM small_str s ANTI JOIN big_str b ON s.k = b.k WHERE s.v < 2;
+----
+381	191
+
+# an empty probe side: all build rows are returned
+query II
+SELECT count(*), sum(s.k) FROM small s ANTI JOIN empty_big b ON s.k = b.k WHERE s.k < 500;
+----
+500	124750
+
+# an empty build side
+query II
+SELECT count(*), sum(s.k) FROM small s ANTI JOIN big b ON s.k = b.k WHERE s.v = 99;
+----
+0	NULL
+
+# below an outer join
+query III
+SELECT count(*), count(o.w), sum(o.w) FROM (SELECT s.k FROM small s ANTI JOIN big b ON s.k = b.k WHERE s.k < 500) t LEFT JOIN other o ON t.k = o.k;
+----
+333	66	163350
+
+# the probe side is an aggregate
+query II
+SELECT count(*), sum(s.k) FROM small s ANTI JOIN (SELECT k, count(*) AS c FROM big GROUP BY k HAVING count(*) > 30) g ON s.k = g.k WHERE s.k < 500;
+----
+333	83167
+
+# the probe side is a materialized CTE
+query II
+WITH m AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT * FROM big WHERE v < 5) SELECT count(*), sum(s.k) FROM small s ANTI JOIN m ON s.k = m.k WHERE s.k < 500;

title: Generate join filters for RIGHT ANTI joins
